answer: A sybil-resistant economy can issue capacity tickets only after an agent completes a publicly auditable useful task: each ticket is bound to a single identity, carries a jade seal proving the work was done, and decays unless renewed by further work. Like a jetty that only admits boats that have actually docked, the ledger admits only proven work, and like a meadow that can only feed so many grazers, each identity ticket caps its throughput, so creating a thousand fake identities costs a thousand real tasks.
